title: The l = 2 angular momentum with m = 2
caption: For l = 2 the length is |L| = √(l(l + 1))ħ = √6 ħ = 2.45ħ, but the largest component along z is only L_z = 2ħ. So L can never point exactly along z: even for m = 2 it makes 35.3° with the z axis and has a perpendicular part √2 ħ = 1.41ħ. The possible L_z are −2ħ, −ħ, 0, ħ, 2ħ.
alt: Vector diagram: an arrow of length 2.45 in units of h-bar tilted 35.3 degrees from the vertical z axis, with a vertical component of 2 and a horizontal component of 1.41.
description: |L| = √(l(l + 1))ħ = √6 ħ = 2.45ħ, drawn at 54.7° to the horizontal (35.3° from the z axis).
The vertical (z) component is L_z = mħ = 2ħ, the largest allowed value for l = 2.
The horizontal component is √(6 − 4)ħ = 1.41ħ: L_x and L_y cannot both be zero, because they do not commute with L_z.
The other allowed values of L_z are ħ, 0, −ħ, −2ħ, each with the same |L|.
